1. **packages/fullstack/src/plugin.ts (`no-split-css` load handler) / PR description** — The PR claims "Works in both dev and build modes," a manifest (`__no_split_css__`), and checks off "✅ Build mode generates proper manifest structure," but the actual code simply does `if (this.environment.mode !== "dev") return "export default [];"`. No build-mode collection or manifest integration exists anywhere in the diff. Either implement build-mode support as described, or rewrite the PR description/checklist so it doesn't claim tested functionality that isn't there — shipping docs that promise build support for an experimental API that silently no-ops in production is misleading.

2. **packages/fullstack/README.md** — The new comparison table states `no-split-css` supports "Dev + Build: ✅ Both," directly contradicting the note two paragraphs below it: "Only works in dev mode (returns empty array in build mode)." Fix this internal contradiction before merge.

3. **packages/fullstack/src/plugin.ts (`no-split-css` load handler)** — The virtual module `\0virtual:fullstack/no-split-css` is loaded once and cached in the dev module graph like any other module; there's no invalidation wired up (e.g. in `hotUpdate`/`handleHotUpdate`) to re-trigger `load()` as new routes/CSS get added to the graph during subsequent requests. This means the collected CSS list can go stale after the first render, undermining the "HMR-compatible"/"collect all CSS at this point" guarantee. Add explicit invalidation of this module id whenever the server module graph changes.

4. **packages/fullstack/src/plugin.ts (`collectCssFromModule`)** — The outer loop already iterates every entry in `environment.moduleGraph.idToModuleMap.values()` directly, so the recursive walk over `mod.importedModules` inside `collectCssFromModule` never does any real filtering (everything gets visited either way) — it's dead code relative to the stated "recursively traverses the server module graph" design. Worse, this means stale/orphaned modules (e.g. CSS from an import that was later removed but whose node wasn't pruned) can leak into the result. Either traverse from the actual rendered entry module(s) to get a real reachability-based collection, or drop the misleading recursion and document that this returns "all CSS ever loaded into the graph," not "all CSS reachable from this render."

5. **Test coverage** — No automated tests were added for the new virtual module (flag-off default behavior, dev collection correctness, client-environment no-op, HMR id attributes). The PR relies solely on "manually tested" claims. Given the rest of the `fullstack` package has test coverage for the `?assets` machinery, this new experimental-but-merged API should get at least a basic unit/e2e test before merge.

6. **packages/fullstack/src/plugin.ts (`no-split-css` load handler, minor)** — `const hrefs = [...cssIds].map(...)` followed by indexing into a second `[...cssIds]` spread inside the next `.map` is redundant and relies on Set iteration order staying identical across two separate spreads. Simplify to build the array once (`const ids = [...cssIds]`) and derive both `href` and `data-vite-dev-id` from it in a single pass.
